source.title: PARTS-EVIDENCE-001 — Exact-model compatibility graph and source resilience
source.body:
## Why this matters

The existing washer sourcing snapshot can detect that a generic parts-catalogue probe is not proof of fit, but does not yet provide a reusable, multi-family evidence graph for part ↔ exact model/revision ↔ market/serial window relationships. Wrong-fit claims cause wasted shipping, failed repairs and potentially safety-critical substitutions. Similar model names, photographs, seller listings, or shared service contracts do not establish compatibility.

## Paradigm shift

Treat compatibility as a versioned, evidence-backed claim with a scoped predicate—not a property inferred from brand/model similarity. Keep fit, interface/electrical ratings, functional behavior, safety qualification, and configuration/firmware constraints as separate dimensions. Support positive and negative observations; absence of evidence stays unknown rather than incompatible. Permit exact-model manufacturer evidence to establish a catalog/listing relation only, not automatically physical fit, function, or safety qualification.

## Proposed benchmark questions

- How often does a part recommendation produce a false-compatible result on a frozen positive/negative/ambiguous test set?
- What fraction of declared common-repair classes have exact-model/revision evidence, and how stale is the evidence?
- What is the wrong-order/return/rework rate and time to locate a correct part?
- How many genuinely independent sources can supply each critical repair class, after distributor ownership/dependency is considered?
- Are service lead-time and affordability claims based on accepted orders and physical delivery rather than listings and advertising?

## Acceptance

- Strict schema, synthetic-only fixture and Rust auditor integrated into the existing appliance audit CLI/workflow.
- Distinguish manufacturer-listed, seller-claimed, cross-reference-inferred, physical-fit-verified, functional-verified, safety-qualified, verified-incompatible and unknown.
- Model suffix/revision/market/serial applicability and supersession windows are explicit.
- No source counts as independent without a declared supplier/distributor dependency identity.
- Mutation tests prevent seller claims from being promoted to functional compatibility, missing evidence becoming incompatibility, expired evidence being presented as current, and one upstream supplier being double-counted.
- No purchase, fit, repair, or safety claim from synthetic fixtures or schema qualification alone.

Reference context: Open Repair Alliance's Oct 2026 dataset reports 619,875 community repair attempts across 34 countries through July 2026. It is useful for repair-event vocabulary and workflow questions, but does not by itself establish South African large-appliance fault prevalence or model-specific part fit. See https://openrepair.org/announcements/over-half-a-million-records-of-open-data-on-repair/ and https://openrepair.org/open-data/downloads/ .

comments.text:
The first implementation is now on draft PR #1827 at exact head `28fb90cc0bba45ec6116537c5de05ebb3b4033f5`:

- [Evidence graph design](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/symtropy/blob/research/large-appliance-repairable-architecture-v0-1/docs/tech/PARTS_COMPATIBILITY_EVIDENCE_GRAPH_V0_1.md)
- [Schema](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/symtropy/blob/research/large-appliance-repairable-architecture-v0-1/schemas/appliances/parts_compatibility_evidence_graph_v0_1.schema.json)
- [Synthetic fixture](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/symtropy/blob/research/large-appliance-repairable-architecture-v0-1/fixtures/appliances/parts_compatibility_evidence_graph_v0_1.json)
- Rust auditor: `tools/household-appliance-bench-audit/src/compatibility.rs` with 13 authored tests; paired CLI flags and workflow integration are included.

The fixture has 9 synthetic compatibility claims, 14 synthetic evidence records, 3 supplier paths and 6 proposed/guardrail benchmarks. It covers seller-only, cross-reference, manufacturer listing, fit-verified, function-verified, independently safety-evidenced, incompatibility, unknown, and supersession states. Two different storefronts share a single upstream source group and correctly count as one delivered source. All records remain synthetic; there are no product-fitment or supply claims.

Exact-head workflow [#39104020413](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/symtropy/actions/runs/39104020413) is queued. The previous baseline commit passed; this new graph is not yet CI-qualified.
